proposals.before: All under heaven was in turmoil; the Grand Commandant obtaining him was like gaining an enemy state."
proposals.after: All under heaven was in turmoil; the Grand General obtaining him was like gaining an enemy state."
proposals.reason: Chinese has 大將軍 (Grand General), but the literal renders it as Grand Commandant, which mismatches the source title.

proposals.before: The hundred offices and responsible officials uphold the law and receive orders, thereby cultivating their duties; for dereliction of duty there is execution, for encroaching on another's office there is punishment."
proposals.after: The hundred offices and responsible officials uphold the law and receive orders, thereby cultivating their duties; for dereliction of duty there is execution, for encroaching on another's office there is punishment.
proposals.reason: Literal English ends with an extraneous closing quotation mark not justified by the Chinese sentence.

proposals.before: Those seated were in the hundreds; all left their mats and prostrated themselves—only Hu alone sat square facing east, addressing Yi by his courtesy name: "How goes the young lord's eminence!"
proposals.after: Those seated were in the hundreds; all left their mats and prostrated themselves—only Hu alone sat square facing east, addressing Yi by name: "How goes the young lord's eminence!"
proposals.reason: 字謂 here marks familiar address; 邑 is Yi's given name, so 'by his courtesy name' misstates the naming form.

proposals.before: Halfway to a banquet he heard an old woman he knew lay dying of fever in the lane.
proposals.after: Someone once invited Yuan She to a banquet; as he entered the ward gate, a guest reported that a mother known to Yuan She was ill and staying in a ward house to avoid contagion.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents 'halfway,' 'old woman,' 'dying of fever'; Chinese only has an invitation, entering the gate, and a report that a known mother was ill and avoiding contagion in a ward house.

proposals.before: Wang Yougong, a county clerk who hated Yuan She, warned Yin, "Humiliate him now and when a real prefect arrives you will crawl back as a clerk while his nameless killers haunt you.
proposals.after: Yuan She had befriended Qi Taibo, a rich man of Xinfeng; Taibo's uterine younger brother Wang Yougong had long envied Yuan She and was then a county gate clerk; he said to Yin, "You as acting prefect have humiliated Yuan She like this—once a true prefect arrives, you will go back as a mansion clerk in a single cart, while Yuan She's assassins are like clouds and kill without anyone knowing the master's name—enough to chill the heart.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits the Qi Taibo friendship and uterine-brother link that the Chinese states, and compresses Wang Yougong's warning so the named relationships are lost.

proposals.before: Rebel chiefs who knew his name hunted him down to pay homage.
proposals.after: Rebel chiefs who had long heard Yuan She's name vied to ask where Prefect Yuan was and paid court to him.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 爭問原尹何在, the explicit search for Prefect Yuan by title.

proposals.before: Yuan She bolted; Shentu Jian, shamed and furious, announced, "I meant to hold the capital with Yuan Juxian—I would not trade him for one clerk!"
proposals.after: Yuan She wished to flee; Shentu Jian inwardly hated and was shamed by him, and pretended, "I wish to share guarding the Three Adjuncts with Yuan Juxian—how could I exchange him for one clerk!"
proposals.reason: Chinese 陽言 marks feigned speech; idiomatic 'announced' loses the false/pretended force.

decisions.after: All under heaven was in turmoil; for the Grand General to obtain him was like gaining an enemy state.
decisions.reason: Focus unit has 大將軍, not 太尉; the prior literal wrongly borrows Grand Commandant from s0043. The proposal fixes the title but still ends with an extraneous closing quote absent from this narrator sentence.

decisions.reason: 字謂邑曰 marks familiar address to Yi; 邑 is his given name (商子邑), and the spoken form is 公子, so 'by his courtesy name' is wrong and 'by name' still overstates the naming form used in the quote.

decisions.after: Someone once invited Yuan She to a banquet. As he entered the ward gate, a guest told him that the mother of a family he knew was ill and had moved to a house within the ward in hopes of escaping the sickness.
decisions.reason: The prior idiomatic invents halfway progress, an old woman, dying of fever, and a lane setting. The worker identified the problem, but its phrase 'a mother known to Yuan She' was unclear; the context is a family he knew whose mother was ill.

decisions.after: Yuan She had befriended Qi Taibo, a wealthy man of Xinfeng. Taibo's younger maternal half brother, Wang Yougong, had always resented Yuan She and was then a clerk in the county office. He told Yin, "As acting magistrate, you have humiliated Yuan She. Once the permanent magistrate arrives, you will return alone by cart to your old post as a commandery clerk. Yuan She's assassins are as numerous as clouds, and when they kill, no one ever knows who ordered it. The thought should chill you.
decisions.reason: The prior idiomatic drops the friendship with Qi Taibo, Wang Yougong's relationship to him, and most of the warning. The worker restored those facts, but its proposed English was overly literal. Parallel editions also confirm that the corrupt local graph 寫 should be 與.

decisions.reason: Chinese 爭問原尹何在 explicitly has the rebels asking where Prefect Yuan was. The worker restored the omitted search, but 'paid court' was too formal and potentially misleading here.

reviewer.name: Codex source review of Grok 4.5 proposals

proposals.before: Then came the famous lords of the blood—Xinling in Wei, Pingyuan in Zhao, Mengchang in Qi, Chunshen in Chu—who traded on royal connections, bankrolled knights-errant, and honored even petty schemers as honored guests.
proposals.after: Then came the famous lords of the blood—Xinling in Wei, Pingyuan in Zhao, Mengchang in Qi, Chunshen in Chu—who traded on royal connections, vied to act as knights-errant, and honored even petty cock-crow dog-thieves as guests.
proposals.reason: Chinese 競為遊俠 means the Four Lords themselves competed in practicing knight-errantry, not that they merely bankrolled others.

proposals.before: Unless an enlightened king is above, surveying them with likes and dislikes, aligning them with ritual and law, how can the people know prohibition and return to rectitude!"
proposals.after: Unless an enlightened king is above, surveying them with likes and dislikes, aligning them with ritual and law, how can the people know prohibition and return to rectitude!
proposals.reason: Stray closing quotation mark has no matching opener in this unit; Zengzi's quotation ended in s0018.

proposals.before: In an empire in turmoil, securing Ju Meng was like gaining an enemy state.
proposals.after: In an empire in turmoil, for the Grand General to obtain him was like gaining an enemy state.
proposals.reason: Chinese 大將軍得之 makes the Grand General the subject who obtained Ju Meng; the idiomatic omits that subject.

proposals.before: As for such as the Yao clan of the northern road, the various Du of the western road, Qiu Jing of the southern road, Prince Yu of Zhao Tuo of the eastern road, Zhao Diao of Nanyang and their sort—mere Robber Zhis dwelling among the people—how are they worth speaking of!
proposals.after: As for such as the Yao clan of the northern road, the various Du of the western road, Qiu Jing of the southern road, Zhao Tuoyu Gongzi of the eastern road, Zhao Diao of Nanyang and their sort—mere Robber Zhis dwelling among the people—how are they worth speaking of!
proposals.reason: 東道趙佗羽公子 is one personal name (Zhao Tuoyu Gongzi), not 'Prince Yu of Zhao Tuo'; the literal rendering splits the name into a false title-and-polity reading.

proposals.before: Yang Jizhu's son, a county clerk, blocked the convoy, so Guo Xie's nephew took the man's head.
proposals.after: Yang Jizhu's son, a county clerk, blocked the convoy, so Guo Xie's elder brother's son took the man's head.
proposals.reason: Chinese 解兄子 is specifically the elder brother's son; idiomatic 'nephew' erases the distinction from the earlier 解姊子 (sister's son) in this same biography.

proposals.before: Still, men like Fan Zhongzi in Chang'an, Zhao Wangsun in Huaili, Gao Gongzi in Changling, Guo Wengzhong west of the river, Lu Wengru in Taiyuan, Er Changqing in Linhuai, and Chen Junru in Dongyang wore the knight's label yet behaved with courteous restraint.
proposals.after: Still, men like Fan Zhongzi in Chang'an, Zhao Wangsun in Huaili, Gao Gongzi in Changling, Guo Wengzhong of Xihe, Lu Wengru in Taiyuan, Er Changqing in Linhuai, and Chen Junru in Dongyang wore the knight's label yet behaved with courteous restraint.
proposals.reason: Chinese 西河郭翁中 is Guo Wengzhong of Xihe (West of the River as a place name); idiomatic 'west of the river' demotes the place-name attachment and is less precise than the parallel residence formulas.

proposals.before: Wang Mang was delighted, recalled Lou Hu to court as former Director of Shining Brightness, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xixiang, and ranked him among the Nine Ministers.
proposals.after: Wang Mang was delighted, recalled Lou Hu to court as Director of Front Shining Brightness, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xixiang, and ranked him among the Nine Ministers.
proposals.reason: 前煇光 is the office title Front Shining Brightness; 前 is part of the name, not the adjective 'former'.

proposals.before: Mang was greatly pleased, summoned Hu to serve as former Director of Shining Brightness, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xixiang, and ranked him among the Nine Ministers.
proposals.after: Mang was greatly pleased, summoned Hu to serve as Director of Front Shining Brightness, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xixiang, and ranked him among the Nine Ministers.
proposals.reason: Same office-title error: 前煇光 should not be rendered 'former Director'.

proposals.before: During Mang's regency the Huaili rebels Zhao Peng and Huo Hong overran the district under Lou Hu's ministry; he lost his post and became a commoner.
proposals.after: During Mang's regency the Huaili rebels Zhao Peng and Huo Hong overran the jurisdiction of the Director of Front Shining Brightness; he lost his post and became a commoner.
proposals.reason: 前煇光界 is that office's jurisdiction; 'former' misreads 前 in the title.

proposals.before: When Mang held the regency, great bandits of Huaili such as Zhao Peng and Huo Hong rose in groups, extending into the former Director of Shining Brightness's jurisdiction; Hu sat guilty and was dismissed to commoner status.
proposals.after: When Mang held the regency, great bandits of Huaili such as Zhao Peng and Huo Hong rose in groups, extending into the Director of Front Shining Brightness's jurisdiction; Hu sat guilty and was dismissed to commoner status.
proposals.reason: Same 前煇光 office-name mistranslation in the literal English.

proposals.before: Chen Zun lost his father young and served with Zhang Song as a Metropolitan clerk.
proposals.after: Chen Zun lost his father young and served with Zhang Song, courtesy Bosong, as a Metropolitan clerk.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits Zhang Song's courtesy name 伯松 present in the Chinese and literal.

proposals.before: A provincial inspector once needed an audience at the Secretariat but found Chen Zun mid-orgy; he crawled to Mistress Chen, kowtowed, explained his deadline, and she smuggled him out the back gate while her son reeled.
proposals.after: A provincial inspector once needed an audience at the Secretariat but found Chen Zun mid-drinking; he went in to Chen Zun's mother, kowtowed, explained his deadline, and she smuggled him out the back gate while her son was soaked in drink.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents 'mid-orgy' for 方飲 (just then drinking) and replaces 遵母 with the invented label 'Mistress Chen'.

proposals.before: Another Chen shared his name; whenever that man announced "Chen Menggong" at a door the room jumped—then groaned when the wrong Chen walked in, so wits dubbed him "Chen Who Frightens the Seats."
proposals.after: Another Chen shared his surname and courtesy name; whenever that man announced "Chen Menggong" at a door the room jumped—then groaned when the wrong Chen walked in, so wits dubbed him "Chen Who Frightens the Seats."
proposals.reason: Chinese 同姓字 means shared surname and courtesy/personal-name forms, not merely 'his name'.

proposals.before: Chen Zun's first act in office was to roll a curtain cart into a back lane, join Widow Zuo's singing party, dance on the rafters, collapse drunk among the cushions, and spend the night carried off by her maids.
proposals.after: Chen Zun's first act in office was to roll a curtain cart into a back lane, join widow Zuo Ajun's singing party, dance leaping the beam, collapse drunk among the cushions, and spend the night carried off by her maids.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops the widow's given name 阿君 present in the Chinese 左阿君.

proposals.before: Shi Dan recommended him for a tough magistracy; at twenty-odd he took Gukou.
proposals.after: Grand Minister of Education Shi Dan recommended him as able to govern a difficult county; at twenty-odd he became magistrate of Gukou.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 大司徒 and compresses 能治劇／谷口令; restore the office title and magistracy wording from the Chinese.

proposals.before: Back at the party he told the crowd, "A mother lies unburied—how can I swallow your wine!
proposals.after: Back at the party he told the crowd, "A parent lies unburied—how can I swallow your wine!
proposals.reason: Chinese 人親 means a parent/kinsman, not specifically a mother; idiomatic over-narrows the kinship term.

proposals.before: He guarded the empress dowager tomb detail as earth-return colonel.
proposals.after: At the funeral of the Literary Mother Empress Dowager, he served as colonel of the earth-returning work.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops the source designation 文母 and flattens 文母太后喪時／守復土校尉; restore the titled dowager and office.

proposals.before: Like Guo Xie he smiled in public and nursed killers within.
proposals.after: Like Guo Xie, he was outwardly warm, benevolent, and modest, while inwardly he concealed a love of killing.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents 'smiled' and 'nursed killers' and drops 溫仁謙遜 / 好殺; align with the Chinese and the literal.

proposals.before: Wang Mang hauled him in, scolded his record, then pardoned him and named him both Pacification governor and Grand Administrator of Tianshui.
proposals.after: Wang Mang hauled him in, scolded his record, then pardoned him and appointed him Grand Guardian of the Pacified Rong (Grand Administrator of Tianshui).
proposals.reason: 鎮戎大尹天水太守 is Wang Mang's renamed single Tianshui post, not two concurrent offices; 'both' misreads the apposition.

proposals.before: Wang Mang stranded officials who clung to him lived.
proposals.after: Wang Mang's provincial shepherds and envoys who attached themselves to Yuan She all survived.
proposals.reason: 'Stranded' invents a meaning absent from 州牧使者依附涉者皆得活; the survivors are Mang's officials who clung to Yuan She.

decisions.after: Then came the famous lords of the blood: Xinling in Wei, Pingyuan in Zhao, Mengchang in Qi, and Chunshen in Chu. Trading on royal connections, they competed in knight-errantry and received even men of the pettiest talents as honored guests.
decisions.reason: The proposal correctly restores the Four Lords as the practitioners of knight-errantry, but its cock-crow dog-thieves wording is too literal for the idiomatic line.
